claim: On host macos-m5pro-20260924 (Apple M5 Pro, 18 cores, 24 GB unified memory, macOS arm64), gitleaks 8.30.1 (the catalog pin) reported its version and ran the same redacted one-commit scan, gitleaks git --no-banner --redact --log-opts=-1, three times. Negative controls: the latest commit of a scratch clone of this repository (repository config) and the clean first commit of a throwaway repository under $TMPDIR each gave no leaks (exit 0). Positive control: after the throwaway repository committed gitleaks' documented sidekiq-secret test fixture, the same scan exited 1 with exactly one finding. That command asserts both gitleaks' exit 1 and 'leaks found: 1' and exits 0 only when both hold, and all commands exit 0. gitleaks is installed through mise and pinned outside this repository: command -v gitleaks resolves to mise's gitleaks 8.30.1 install, and the host's mise global config pins gitleaks = "8.30.1" (both in the first command's output).
limitations: Each scan covers one commit (--log-opts=-1): the scratch clone's latest commit (the recorded catalog_revision), then the throwaway repository's clean commit and its fixture commit. None is a full-history or working-tree scan, and a clean result does not prove that no secret exists.

The scratch-clone scan used this repository's .gitleaks.toml, which extends the default rules. The throwaway repository has no config, so its two scans used gitleaks' default rules. The host's control plane also runs gitleaks on staged changes before each commit; this receipt does not cover that hook.

Positive control: the fixture is the sidekiq-secret example from gitleaks' own README and rule tests (two fixed hex words), not a real credential. The command builds it at run time from split pieces, so the value never appears in this receipt, and every scan ran with --redact. The throwaway commits used core.hooksPath=/dev/null (the host's pre-commit gitleaks hook would otherwise block the fixture commit), commit.gpgsign=false and a fixed probe identity. The positive-control command's own exit is 0 only when gitleaks exits 1 and reports exactly one leak, and its output keeps gitleaks' log lines and exit code. A pre-check with gitleaks stdin and a JSON report, which is not part of this receipt, found one sidekiq-secret finding.
